get.description: Read from what Dev flow stored and never from GitHub. attention is true when the caller has a pull request, waiting or stopped, that is not sent back, a stopped project, a card of Dev flow's whose pull request waits, a GitHub link that has expired, or a Claude login due for renewal within a month or past it, and false otherwise. The nav bar asks it with the session's cookie. Without a valid token, 401 with an empty body.
get.summary: Whether something needs the caller, for the nav bar

delete.description: Forgets the login and its sealed token. 204, whether or not there was one. Without a valid token, 401 with an empty body; a change from another origin, 403.

get.description: Whether one is set, when it was given and renew_by, a year after; state is none, ok, due_soon from 31 days before renew_by, or expired from renew_by on. Never the token or any part of it. Without a valid token, 401 with an empty body; a change from another origin, 403.

put.description: The token from claude setup-token, sealed in the vault and replacing any before it, given now, so its year starts again. The space around it is dropped. Answers the status it leaves, never the token. 422 for anything that does not look like a setup token, sk-ant-oat followed by more visible characters, and nothing is stored; Dev flow does not ask Anthropic whether it works. Without a valid token, 401 with an empty body; a change from another origin, 403.
put.summary: Give Dev flow the caller's Claude login

get.description: Read from what Dev flow stored and never from GitHub. waiting, the pull requests that wait for the caller and were not sent back, the runner's and Dev flow's own cards'; stopped, those the runner stopped on, not sent back, and the caller's projects stopped because something landed on their default branch that Dev flow did not put there; projects, how many the caller has connected; stale, whether any project is stale or failing, as the waiting list says them; needs_relink, whether the caller's GitHub link has expired; and claude_login, where their Claude login stands, none, ok, due_soon or expired, as GET /devflow/api/claude-login says it. The core calls it with the user's token in the Authorization header. Without a valid token, 401 with an empty body.
get.summary: What waits, for the front page

delete.description: Removes the account, its two tokens and any link started. Nothing is revoked at the code host. Without a valid token, 401 with an empty body; from another origin, 403.

post.description: Stores a single use state and a PKCE verifier for ten minutes, and answers the code host's address to send the browser to, carrying the state and the S256 challenge. The code host sends the browser back to /devflow/github/callback. Without a valid token, 401 with an empty body; from another origin, 403.
post.summary: Start linking the caller's GitHub account

get.description: Every installation of the app the caller's GitHub account can reach, read as them, with the account it is on and its repositories, sorted by name, each saying whether it is already a project; and install_url, where to install the app. 409 when GitHub is not linked or the link has expired, 503 when GitHub did not answer. Without a valid token, 401 with an empty body; a change from another origin, 403.
get.summary: The repositories the caller can connect

get.description: Needs no token. It answers whenever the process serves, and says nothing about what Dev flow depends on.
Each connected repository, by owner and name. Without a valid token, 401 with an empty body; a change from another origin, 403.

post.description: Asks GitHub, as the caller, whether the repository is among those of the installation they can reach, and only then stores it, with the owner and name GitHub gave. 201 with the project. 404 for a repository the caller cannot reach through that installation, 409 when it is already a project or GitHub is not linked, 422 naming a missing field, 503 when GitHub did not answer. Without a valid token, 401 with an empty body; a change from another origin, 403.
post.summary: Connect a repository, which makes it a project

delete.description: 204, and everything Dev flow stored for it goes with it. Nothing changes on GitHub. 404 for a project the caller does not have. Without a valid token, 401 with an empty body; a change from another origin, 403.

get.description: Every card of the project as its last read found it, newest change first: its number, title and web_url, its state, the reason it is there, null when there is nothing to say, what it waits for, its priority and changed_at. Read from what Dev flow stored, never from GitHub. 404 for a project the caller does not have. Without a valid token, 401 with an empty body.

The card as last read, its number, title, web_url, state and reason, and its pull_request, number and url, null before one was opened; each of its runs, newest first, with its kind, the worker it was handed to, when it started and finished, how long it took, its result and, for a failure, its reason and whether it lay in the card, the auth method, the tokens in and out, the check's exit code and the last lines of its output, null when it did not run, and the commit it left; the latest report in its form, the latest build's, null when no build has handed one back; and each review, newest first, with the commit the worker reviewed, its verdict, summary, findings, each blocking or not with its file, line, what and why, the reviewer's view on each decision for the owner, when it was recorded, whether its copy is posted, and whether it is current, for the card's head commit; and the screenshots of its head commit, the commit, the pictures' names paired desktop and phone by page, read through getCardScreenshot, and the worker's note, null when its newest build that succeeded tried none. Read from what Dev flow stored, never from GitHub; every text from GitHub or an agent is to be shown as text. 404 for a project or a card the caller does not have. Without a valid token, 401 with an empty body.
get.summary: A card's whole story so far

post.description: Merges a card of Dev flow's own, from Waiting for you, with a merge commit, as the caller's linked GitHub account and never as the app, only while its pull request's head is head_commit, the commit its run built and checked and the page showed. In order: 404 for a project or card the caller does not have; 422 without head_commit; 409 when the card is not waiting for the caller with a pull request; 409 when the project is stopped, since something landed on its default branch that Dev flow did not put there; 409 when head_commit is not the commit the run built, after the project is read again; 409 when GitHub is not linked or the link has expired; then GitHub is asked. 204 once merged and the project read again, which makes the card done. 409 when GitHub says the head moved, after the project is read again, and when GitHub will not merge it or refuses, with its reason; 503 when GitHub did not answer. Without a valid token, 401 with an empty body; a change from another origin, 403.
post.summary: Merge a card's pull request that waits, as the caller

get.description: The PNG the card's newest build that succeeded listed as name, read from the branch pr-screenshots of the project's own repository, at devflow/<number>/<the head commit's first seven characters>/<name>.png, as the app. Always image/png, with X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none' and Cache-Control: private, max-age=3600. 404 for a project or card the caller does not have, a card with no such build, or a name the build did not list, without asking GitHub; 404 when GitHub has no such file; 502 when what GitHub has is not a PNG or is over 5 MB; 503 when GitHub did not answer. Without a valid token, 401 with an empty body.
get.summary: One of the pictures the worker took of a card's head commit, read from GitHub as the app

post.description: Posts comment, trimmed and with nothing added, on the card's open pull request as the caller's linked GitHub account and never as the app; the read of the project that follows takes it, as any comment of his past the newest already taken, and starts a fix run with it, which is not a review round. In order: 404 for a project or card the caller does not have; 422 when comment is missing, empty once trimmed, or longer than 10,000 characters; 409 when the card neither waits for the caller nor has stopped, or has no open pull request; 409 when GitHub is not linked or the link has expired; then GitHub is asked. 204 once posted and the project read again. 409 when GitHub refuses, with its reason; 503 when GitHub did not answer. Without a valid token, 401 with an empty body; a change from another origin, 403.
post.summary: Send a card of Dev flow's own back, with a comment as the caller

post.description: 204 once it has been read, whether or not GitHub answered, which the list then says; 202 when the read is still under way after 10 seconds, and it goes on. 404 for a project the caller does not have. Without a valid token, 401 with an empty body; a change from another origin, 403.
post.summary: Read a project from GitHub now

post.description: Accepts commit, the commit the page showed the project stopped by, and records who resumed it, when, and that commit, so the project hands out work again. In order: 404 for a project the caller does not have; 422 when commit is missing or is not a full commit id; 409 when it is not stopped; 409 when it is stopped by another commit than commit, which landed since the page was shown. 204 once resumed. Without a valid token, 401 with an empty body; a change from another origin, 403.
post.summary: Resume a stopped project, accepting what landed on its default branch

get.description: The labels that pick and hold its cards and mark what needs the caller, and whether a card's pull request waits for them, never or always. 404 for a project the caller does not have. Without a valid token, 401 with an empty body; a change from another origin, 403.

put.description: Takes all four and answers them as saved. A label is written, at most 50 characters, with no space at either end and no comma, and the three are different names whatever their case; waits_for_owner is never or always. 422 naming each field that breaks a rule, 404 for a project the caller does not have. Without a valid token, 401 with an empty body; a change from another origin, 403.

post.description: A new key for the project's workers, answered this once with save_command, the command that saves it in ~/.devflow/<project>.env for the start command to read: Dev flow keeps only its SHA-256 and never shows it again. It replaces the project's last key at once, so a worker holding that one is refused from then on. 404 for a project the caller does not have. Without a valid token, 401 with an empty body; a change from another origin, 403.

get.description: Every worker that has said hello with the project's key, by when it first did, with what it reported, when it was last seen, and rebuild: recipe when it runs another version of the recipe than Dev flow last read, base_image when it runs on another base image than the one released, or null; key_made_at, when the project's key was made, null before one has been; recipe_version, the recipe's version as last read, null before then or when the default branch has none; start_command, the command that builds and starts the project's worker; and held, why the project hands out no work whichever worker asks, the first that applies: stopped, when something landed on its default branch that Dev flow did not put there, unwatched, when its default branch has not been read for five minutes, no_claude_login when its user has given no Claude login, claude_login_expired when it is past its renewal, or null. The key itself is never in it. 404 for a project the caller does not have. Without a valid token, 401 with an empty body; a change from another origin, 403.

code_host is fake when GitHub is faked, which every Dev flow page then says in a banner, and github otherwise. github.state is none, linked or needs_relink, with the login it was linked as, null with none. Without a valid token, 401 with an empty body.
get.summary: Which code host Dev flow talks to, and the caller's GitHub link

get.description: Read from what Dev flow stored and never from GitHub. items are the pull requests that are the caller's turn in every project, by project and number; own_items are Dev flow's own, read from its own tables, in this part each a project stopped because something landed on its default branch that Dev flow did not put there, with the commit, who did it, when, and the commit's address on GitHub, by project; cards are Dev flow's own cards whose pull requests wait for the caller, each with its pull request, the head commit its run built and checked, the branch it merges into, the report's summary, the decisions the agent marked for the caller with the count of the others, the check Dev flow ran, review, the reviewer's verdict on its head commit with its summary and how many findings block, null when it has none, and can_merge, false while the project is stopped, by project and number; count is the items not sent back, the own items and the cards, plus one when needs_relink; projects says for each when it was last read, stale when that is more than five minutes ago or never, and failing when its last read failed. Without a valid token, 401 with an empty body.
get.summary: What waits for the caller, as last read

post.description: Merges with a merge commit, as the caller's linked GitHub account, only while the pull request's head is head_commit, the commit the page showed. In order: 404 for an item the caller does not have; 422 without head_commit; 409 when it is stopped, sent back, or its checks are not green; 409 when head_commit is not the stored head; 409 when GitHub is not linked or the link has expired; then GitHub is asked. 204 once merged and the project read again. 409 when GitHub says the head moved, after the project is read again, and when GitHub will not merge it or refuses, with its reason; 503 when GitHub did not answer. Without a valid token, 401 with an empty body; a change from another origin, 403.
post.summary: Merge a waiting pull request, as the caller

get.description: The PNG the item's pull request body showed as name, read from the branch pr-screenshots of the item's own repository, at <number>/<name>.png, as the app. Always image/png, with X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none' and Cache-Control: private, max-age=3600. 404 for an item the caller does not have, or a name its body did not show, without asking GitHub; 404 when GitHub has no such file; 502 when what GitHub has is not a PNG or is over 5 MB; 503 when GitHub did not answer. Without a valid token, 401 with an empty body.
get.summary: One of a waiting item's screenshots, read from GitHub as the app

post.description: Posts comment, trimmed and with nothing added, on the pull request as the caller's linked GitHub account, which the runner reads as the owner's input on its next turn. In order: 404 for an item the caller does not have; 422 when comment is missing, empty once trimmed, or longer than 10,000 characters; 409 when GitHub is not linked or the link has expired; then GitHub is asked. 204 once posted, with the item marked sent back at once and the project read again. 409 when GitHub refuses, with its reason; 503 when GitHub did not answer. Without a valid token, 401 with an empty body; a change from another origin, 403.
post.summary: Send a waiting or stopped pull request back, with a comment as the caller

get.description: From the token alone. Without a valid token, 401 with an empty body.
get.summary: The account the request's token names

post.description: The worker's id, a UUID it made when it started, its name, the container's hostname, and the recipe version and base image it runs. Records the worker in the key's project, or brings it up to date, and marks it seen. 204. 422 naming a field that is missing or breaks a rule: every one is required, and each text is at most 255 characters. Takes the project's worker key as Authorization: Bearer dfw_…, and nothing else: without a key the project has now, 401 with an empty body. No Origin is needed, and no cookie is read or set.

Marks the worker seen and answers its next job, 200 with Cache-Control: no-store: the first of its project's queued cards that waits for nothing, by priority, high, none, low, then oldest first, moved to building, with a run recorded for this worker. The job holds the card, the repository, the branch, the brief, the report's schema, the check, the run's user's Claude token, a push key narrowed to the repository and its expiry, the committer and the limits. 204 when there is no work for it: a project that is stopped, or whose default branch has not been watched for five minutes, no card to take, a user without a Claude login or with one past its renewal, a worker that needs a rebuild, running another version of the recipe than Dev flow last read or another base image than the one released, or the code host not answering what a job needs, such as the project's .devflow/project.json. 409 for a worker that has not said hello in the key's project, which says hello and asks again; 422 without worker_id. Takes the project's worker key as Authorization: Bearer dfw_…, and nothing else: without a key the project has now, 401 with an empty body. No Origin is needed, and no cookie is read or set.

With state checking, the agent has finished and the check runs: the card moves from building to checking. 204. Only for the worker holding the job, named by worker_id, while it runs; 404 for any other worker, a job that is not one of the project's, or one that has finished. 422 without worker_id, or with a state that is not checking. Takes the project's worker key as Authorization: Bearer dfw_…, and nothing else: without a key the project has now, 401 with an empty body. No Origin is needed, and no cookie is read or set.

A new push key for the job's repository, narrowed to fetching and pushing code, with when it expires, 200 with Cache-Control: no-store, since a key lasts an hour and a run up to 90 minutes. Only for the worker holding the job, named by worker_id, while the job runs; 404 for any other worker, a job that is not one of the project's, or one that has finished. 503 when the code host made no key now, which the worker asks for again; 422 without worker_id. Takes the project's worker key as Authorization: Bearer dfw_…, and nothing else: without a key the project has now, 401 with an empty body. No Origin is needed, and no cookie is read or set.
post.summary: A fresh push key for a running job

post.description: What the worker sends when its job ends, whatever happened: outcome, succeeded with the agent's report or failed with the failure's reason and whether it lies in the card; the check's exit code and the last 200 lines of its output, null when it did not run; the branch, which must be the job's, and its head commit; the auth method; Claude's usage as it came, an object; the duration in milliseconds; the last 200 lines of stderr; and permission_denials, the actions the agent was refused, an array or null. Each is stored on the run as it came. A build's report is read against contracts/devflow/report.schema.json, and one that does not match is a failure in the card; a review's report is its verdict, read against contracts/devflow/verdict.schema.json, and one that does not match is a failure in the run, never a verdict. A review's head_commit is the commit it was handed, or null on a failure; any other is 422. A failure outside the card puts the card back in queued, counting nothing against it; a failure in the card, a report that does not match, a report that stopped, a check that did not run or failed stop it with why; otherwise the card waits, checked, for its pull request. 204. Only for the worker holding the job while it runs, and once; 404 otherwise. 422 naming a field that is missing or breaks a rule. Takes the project's worker key as Authorization: Bearer dfw_…, and nothing else: without a key the project has now, 401 with an empty body. No Origin is needed, and no cookie is read or set.

get.description: The file .devflow/Dockerfile of the key's project, from its repository's default branch, read as the app at the newest commit that changed it: text/plain, with that commit's id in X-Devflow-Recipe-Version, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and Cache-Control: no-store. 404 when the repository has none; 422 naming the line when it copies files into the image, a COPY or an ADD in any case, after continued lines are joined, or when it is not UTF-8 text of at most 64 KB; 503 when GitHub did not answer. Takes the project's worker key as Authorization: Bearer dfw_…, and nothing else: without a key the project has now, 401 with an empty body.
get.summary: The project's recipe, to build a worker from
